the case was remanded Sine Die, and accused detained
in custody. During the period of remand, the accused
was charged with Possession of Inflammatory Literature

case was remanded for judgment until 1.9.36. at 2:30
p.m. On the 1.9.36. judgment was rendered and the
accused sentenced to 2 years and 6 months' imprisonment
for forming a body with intent to injure the Republic
of China. Seized literature confiscated.

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by [签名]

With reference to the case against Tsang Ching Sz
arrested on Gordon Road on July 19, 1936 in possession of a
quantity of communistic literature, I have to report that
a thorough interrogation of the accused has failed to reveal
any further information.

The accused expressed his willingness to assist
the Municipal Police in effecting the arrest of one "Sheng"
who had handed him the literature which he had in his possession
when arrested. He and Sheng were in the habit of meeting
each other at noon every Tuesday and Friday at Nanking and
Fokien Roads corner, and an opportunity was afforded Tsang
to be present at this rendezvous at the appointed time on
Tuesday, July 21, 1936 in order that he could contact Sheng,
leaving us to effect his arrest. However, although Tsang
waited at the appointed place for some forty minutes, Sheng
failed to materialize. This was probably due to the fact
that the vernacular press had carried reports on July 20, 1936
giving details of Tsang's arrest.

The accused steadfastly maintains that he is not
knowingly connected with any subversive elements and maintains
that he was not aware of the contents of the books given him
since he is unable to read.

He has no relatives or friends in Shanghai that would
enable a check to be made on his statement, and I am of the
opinion that he is telling the truth when he states that Sheng
approached him whilst he was selling newspapers, and that he
unquestioningly jumped at the offer to work for this man as
the money he received from him raised him from a state of penury
to comparative wealth.

主题 关于1936年7月19日在戈登路逮捕的张金士（Tsang Ching Sz）一案。

由 皮茨（Pitts）副探长 制作 转发 [签名]

关于1936年7月19日在戈登路逮捕的持有大量共产主义宣传品的张金士一案，兹报告如下：对被告的彻底审讯未能揭示更多消息。

被告表示愿意协助工部局警务处逮捕一名“沈”，此人曾将他在被捕时持有的宣传品交给他。他和沈习惯在每个星期二和星期五中午在南京路与福建路路口见面，1936年7月21日星期二，在指定时间给予张金士出现在该接头地点的机会，以便他能接触沈，由我们实施逮捕。然而，尽管张金士在指定地点等待了约四十分钟，沈并未出现。这可能是因为1936年7月20日的中文报纸刊登了关于张金士被捕的详细报道。

被告坚决维持其说法，即他并不知情地与任何颠覆分子有关联，并坚持称他不知道交给他的书籍的内容，因为他不识字。

他在上海没有亲戚或朋友可供核实其陈述，我认为他说的是实话，即沈在他卖报时接近他，而他毫不犹豫地接受了为这个人工作的提议，因为从这个人那里得到的钱使他从贫困状态跃升至相对富裕的状态。

Tsang Ching Sz (張金士)
Tungchow (通州)                                   xxx  D.S.I. Prokofiev
Pootoo Rd. Stn.          19/7/36                          Tam Shou Shih (

My name is Tsang Ching Sz (張金士), 22, native of
Tungchow (通...), single, ex-newspaper vendor. I never went
to school and therefore can read and write only a few charac-
ters. I came to Shanghai from my native country about eight
years ago together with my parents. We lived in Chapei. My
parents were killed during the hostilities in Chapei in 1932
and since that time I lived the life of a beggar until about
a year ago when I started to work as a newspaper vendor. My
daily earnings ranged from 30 to 100 coppers. I could not
afford to pay for a regular lodging and therefore have no
fixed abode. In summer I sleep in Soochow Road Public Garden,
or in some alleyway.

About two months ago when I was selling newspapers on
Fokien Road near Nanking Road, a male Chinese, who later gave
me his name as Sheng (沈), approached me and asked me about
the conditions of my life. I replied that my earnings were
very small and that I was very poor and unhappy. Shen then
offered me to sell some newspapers for him and promised to
help me. We agreed to meet at 12 noon at the same place twice
a week. Shen used to give me 30 or 40 cents each time, but
never asked me to do something in return until 10 days ago,
when he gave me two dollars and a parcel. I was instructed
to take the parcel to a certain place in French Town and
deliver it to a person who would approach me and give a pre-
arranged password. I carried out this instructions accordingly.

When Sheng saw me on Friday last, he told me to look
up at the usual place at noon on July 18. When we met again...

我叫张金士，22岁，通州人，未婚，前报贩。我从未上过学，因此只识得几个字。大约八年前，我与父母从家乡来到上海。我们住在闸北。1932年闸北战事期间，我的父母遇害，自那时起我一直过着乞丐的生活，直到大约一年前开始做报贩。我每日的收入在30至100枚铜元之间。因无力支付固定住所的租金，故无固定居所。夏季，我睡在苏州路公共花园，或某些弄堂里。

大约两个月前，当我在南京路附近的福建路卖报时，一名中国男子走近我，他后来告诉我他姓沈 (Sheng)，并询问我的生活状况。我回答说收入微薄，生活贫困且不幸。沈随后提议让我替他卖一些报纸，并承诺会帮助我。我们约定每周两次，中午12点在同一地点见面。沈每次给我30或40分，但直到10天前才要求我作为回报做些事情，当时他给了我两美元和一个包裹。我奉命将包裹送到法租界的某处，交给一个会主动接近我并说出预定暗号的人。我照此指令执行了任务。

上周五沈见到我时，让我于7月18日中午在老地方碰头。当我们再次按预定见面时……

I was instructed to go to No. 330, Gordon Road and to wait on

    while on the way to the above address I was arrested.
I did not know the contents of the parcel and the note. Sheng
only told me to be careful and not to open the parcel, as he
